name: Autosomal Recessive Intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Recessive Intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease

criteria.description: Presence of a progressive distal symmetric sensorimotor neuropathy with distal muscle weakness and atrophy
Nerve conduction studies showing intermediate slowing of motor nerve conduction velocities (25-45 m/s)
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in genes associated with autosomal recessive intermediate CMT (e.g., GDAP1, SH3TC2)
Consistent autosomal recessive inheritance pattern or consanguinity
Predominant distal lower limb muscle atrophy with foot deformities such as pes cavus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal sensorimotor neuropathy with intermediate nerve conduction velocities and confirmation of biallelic pathogenic mutations in relevant genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electrophysiological and genetic testing are essential for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal symmetric muscle weakness and atrophy
searchTerms: weakness and wasting in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intermediate slowing of motor nerve conduction velocity
searchTerms: slower than normal motor nerve signals
moderate slowing of movement nerve conduction

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss including impaired vibration and proprioception
searchTerms: loss of vibration and position sense in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in lower limbs
Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop
muscle cramps in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Foot ulcers secondary to sensory loss
searchTerms: ulcers on feet due to numbness
mild nerve pain in hands and feet
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Nerve ultrasound may show nerve enlargement
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in GDAP1, SH3TC2, or other related genes
other: Electrophysiological studies demonstrating intermediate slowing of motor nerve conduction velocities
Muscle biopsy showing chronic denervation changes

distinguishingFeatures: Typically slower nerve conduction velocities (<38 m/s)
Normal or mildly slowed nerve conduction velocities

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks
Severe sensory loss with ulcerations or infections
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
Orphanet: Autosomal recessive intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. ORPHA:268337.
Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
